newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
President Chandrika Kumaratunga to honour Sri Lankan World Cup champion cricket team's captain Arjuna Ranatunga and manager Duleep Mendis with highest national award "Deshamanya."
Colombo airport opens viewing gallery to public after closing it down for security reasons.
THE ISLAND
Twenty Two Tamil Tiger suspects attempt to break out of jail in eastern Trincomalee. Security forces kill five and rearrest 11 of them. Others escape.
DIVAINA
Former army commander Lt. General Cecil Waidyaratne arrested for allegedly swindling the army of 43 million rupees in food provision deal.
Sri Lanka's annual average inflation for October increased to 15.3 percent from 14.8 percent in the previous month, the Department of Census and Statistics say.
DINAMINA
Thirty year-old taxi driver jailed for 15 months for selling photographs of important buildings in Colombo to separatist Tamil rebels.
Students of Kelaniya University riot and burn bus after it knocked down student at pedestrian crossing.
LANKADEEPA
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) explode land mind on railway track near Valachchenai in the eastern Batticaloa district, destroying five carriages of a goods train.
Army grants another two-week amnesty to deserters. Army says nearly 20,000 soldiers have deserted since the early 1980s when the war against LTTE began.
VEERAKESARI
More than 20,000 soldiers have deserted the army over past 10 years, army commander Lt. General Rohan Daluwatte says.
THINAKARAN

Students in northern Jaffna peninsula boycott classes to protest alleged murder of Tamil girl student and her family by security forces. Securuty forces have taken two soldiers and two policemen into custody for the crime.
-- Colombo newsroom 941-434319
